Only String static arguments are accepted as recipe and constants. A recipe shaped otherwise is not linked and falls back to unsupported, which is a refusal rather than a wrong answer.

proposals.title: Link StringConcatFactory.makeConcat as well
proposals.plainSummary: The sibling factory with no recipe — used when javac concatenates without constant text — is still refused.
proposals.userBenefit: More javac-emitted string concatenation runs instead of being refused, with no new machinery.
proposals.why: makeConcat takes no static arguments: the call site descriptor alone says what to concatenate. The recogniser already keys on the bootstrap's identity, so this is a second constant tuple and a recipe-free path through the same executor.
proposals.tradeoff: Widens what the linker accepts, and each addition makes 'we link one call site' less true. It should stay a short explicit list rather than becoming a registry.

proposals.title: Decide what to do when a linked recipe's arity disagrees with the call site
proposals.plainSummary: If a class file's recipe asks for more arguments than the call site provides, we throw BootstrapMethodError at execution.
proposals.userBenefit: A corrupt or hand-built class file gets a clear diagnosis instead of a confusing one, and the choice is deliberate rather than incidental.
proposals.why: The recipe and the descriptor are two accounts of the same thing, written by the same compiler. Disagreement means the file is wrong, so arguably it belongs in validation at parse time — where it would be a ClassFormatError — rather than as a runtime error on a path that has already started concatenating.
proposals.tradeoff: Moving it to parse time means walking bootstrap arguments during validation, which is the resolution that attribute.rs deliberately avoids. The current runtime check is cheap and correct; the question is only whether the diagnosis is in the right place.

proposals.title: Link LambdaMetafactory.metafactory
proposals.plainSummary: Lambdas and method references still do not run.
proposals.userBenefit: The other half of what javac 9+ emits routinely; today any class containing a lambda is refused at load.
proposals.why: This is the natural next bootstrap, and unlike string concatenation it genuinely needs invoke machinery — a call site that yields a functional-interface instance implies MethodHandle-like dispatch and a synthetic class.
proposals.tradeoff: Large. It cannot reuse the shortcut this round took: the factory's contract is an object, not a string template, so the java.lang.invoke package this round avoided becomes unavoidable.
